tex_content.html:
A focusing base of length at most one has length at most $\delta +\mu $. If focusing triangles have bases in one unit arc and disjoint interiors, the sum of their base lengths is at most $\delta +\mu $.
Proof

↗ lem:focusing-triangle-base-length-bound \sketch Sum the preceding inequality; the base turning totals at most $\delta $, and the disjoint disks have total area at most $\mu $.

□

Lemma
[No sub-geodesic of Dx is a homotopically trivial embedded loop]
